India Squad: Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill(c), Virat Kohli, Ruturaj Gaikwad, KL Rahul(w), Naman Dhir, Ravindra Jadeja, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Gurnoor Brar, Kuldeep Yadav, Prasidh Krishna, Mohammed Siraj, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Auqib Nabi, Dhruv Jurel

12:50 Local Time, 07:20 GMT, 12:50 IST: West Indies looked set for something special in the series opener in Thiruvananthapuram, but that promising start lasted only around an hour and a half before things unravelled. John Campbell and Justin Greaves put on a superb 135 for the first wicket in 19.1 overs after West Indies were asked to bat, briefly putting India under pressure. But once that partnership was broken, the innings lost momentum, with the middle order unable to build on the platform. Amir Jangoo’s unbeaten 58 off 43 took them to 295/7, but it proved well short of what was required on that surface. Under the lights, India made the chase look effortless. Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli made light work of the target, taking India home with 50 balls and eight wickets to spare. West Indies now have their backs against the wall, and they need a win today to keep the series alive. Hello and welcome, everyone, to our live coverage of the second ODI between India and West Indies in Guwahati.

A lot went right for India in Thiruvananthapuram, although there are still a few areas they will want to tighten up. Kuldeep Yadav was the standout, looking in as good a rhythm as he has in recent months and returning superb figures of 4/40. The performance was another reminder of why the left-arm wristspinner should be a regular feature in India’s XI in this format. Shubman Gill continued doing what he has done since making his ODI debut, while Virat Kohli produced a more aggressive version of his usual brilliance. After smashing nine sixes in his unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, Kohli said: “I've got a challenge at this stage of my career to kind of up the ante and play a gear or two higher.” It will be fascinating to see if he carries that approach into this game.

However, Nitish Reddy did not make the desired impact with the new ball, and India will want more from him if they see him as a potential back-up for the injured Hardik Pandya. With wickets up front still a priority, Auqib Nabi or Mohammed Siraj could come into the equation. West Indies, meanwhile, have suffered a setback with Justin Greaves ruled out due to a calf injury, just after he scored his maiden ODI hundred in the series opener. Their bowling also needs a response after a disappointing outing, which could open the door for Vitel Lawes or Shamar Joseph. Can West Indies fight back, or will India take an unassailable lead? We won’t have to wait long, with the toss not too far away.
